For the truth of incident purely personal, it is needless to press any claim, seeing that the hero owns no higher name than that of--A Soldier of Fortune.

arxiv-1805-09868.title: All macroscopic quantum states are fragile and hard to prepare
arxiv-1805-09868.creator: Andrea López Incera, Pavel Sekatski, Wolfgang Dür
arxiv-1805-09868.description: Abstract We study the effect of local decoherence on arbitrary quantum states. Adapting techniques developed in quantum metrology, we show that the action of generic local noise processes –though arbitrarily small– always yields a state whose Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) with respect to local observables is linear in system size N N , independent of the initial state.

arxiv-2003-13983.title: Business disruptions from social distancing
arxiv-2003-13983.creator: Miklós Koren, Rita Pető
arxiv-2003-13983.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Miklós Koren, Rita Pető. Social distancing interventions can be effective against epidemics but are potentially detrimental for the economy. Businesses that rely heavily on face-to-face communication or close physical proximity when producing a product or providing a service are particularly vulnerable. There is, however, no systematic evidence about the role of human interactions across different lines of business and about which will be the most limited by social distancing. Here we provide theory-based measures of the reliance of U.S.

arxiv-2012-15819.title: Transcription-dependent spatial organization of a gene locus
arxiv-2012-15819.creator: Lev Barinov, 1 Sergey Ryabichko, 2 William Bialek, 2,3,4 and Thomas Gregor 2,3,5
arxiv-2012-15819.description: Abstract There is growing appreciation that gene function is connected to the dynamic structure of the chromosome. Here we explore the interplay between three–dimensional structure and transcriptional activity at the single cell level. We show that inactive loci are spatially more compact than active ones, and that within active loci the enhancer driving transcription is closest to the promoter.

arxiv-2112-01442.title: Learning Large-scale Network Embedding from Representative Subgraph
arxiv-2112-01442.creator: Junsheng Kong, Weizhao Li, Ben Liao, Jiezhong Qiu, Chang-Yu (Kim) Hsieh, Yi Cai, Jinhui Zhu, Shengyu Zhang
arxiv-2112-01442.description: Abstract We study the problem of large-scale network embedding, which aims to learn low-dimensional latent representations for network mining applications. Recent research in the field of network embedding has led to significant progress such as DeepWalk, LINE, NetMF, NetSMF. However, the huge size of many real-world networks makes it computationally expensive to learn network embedding from the entire network.

arxiv-2210-01810.title: X-ray Reverberation Mapping of Ark 564 using Gaussian Process Regression
arxiv-2210-01810.creator: Collin Lewin, Erin Kara, Dan Wilkins, Guglielmo Mastroserio, Javier A. García, Rachel C. Zhang, William N. Alston, Riley Connors, Thomas Dauser, Andrew Fabian, Adam Ingram, Jiachen Jiang, Anne Lohfink, Matteo Lucchini, Christopher S. Reynolds, Francesco Tombesi, Michiel van der Klis, Jingyi Wang
arxiv-2210-01810.description: Abstract Ark 564 is an extreme high-Eddington Narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxy, known for being one of the brightest, most rapidly variable soft X-ray AGN, and for having one of the lowest temperature coronae. Here we present a 410 ks NuSTAR observation and two 115 ks XMM-Newton observations of this unique source, which reveal a very strong, relativistically broadened iron line.

arxiv-2301-08577.title: Ontology Pre-training for Poison Prediction
arxiv-2301-08577.creator: Martin Glauer, Fabian Neuhaus, Till Mossakowski, Janna Hastings
arxiv-2301-08577.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Martin Glauer, Fabian Neuhaus, Till Mossakowski, Janna Hastings. Integrating human knowledge into neural networks has the potential to improve their robustness and interpretability. We have developed a novel approach to integrate knowledge from ontologies into the structure of a Transformer network which we call ontology pre-training: we train the network to predict membership in ontology classes as a way to embed the structure of the ontology into the network, and subsequently fine-tune the network for the particular prediction task.

arxiv-2406-17450.title: Pseudo Labelling for Enhanced Masked Autoencoders
arxiv-2406-17450.creator: Srinivasa Rao Nandam, Sara Atito, Zhenhua Feng, Josef Kittler, Muhammad Awais
arxiv-2406-17450.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Srinivasa Rao Nandam, Sara Atito, Zhenhua Feng, Josef Kittler, Muhammad Awais. Masked Image Modeling (MIM)-based models, such as SdAE, CAE, GreenMIM, and MixAE, have explored different strategies to enhance the performance of Masked Autoencoders (MAE) by modifying prediction, loss functions, or incorporating additional architectural components. In this paper, we propose an enhanced approach that boosts MAE performance by integrating pseudo labelling for both class and data tokens, alongside replacing the traditional pixel-level reconstruction with token-level reconstruction.

arxiv-2410-06408.title: Automating Data Science Pipelines with Tensor Completion
arxiv-2410-06408.creator: Shaan Pakala, Bryce Graw, Dawon Ahn, Tam Dinh, Mehnaz Tabassum Mahin, Vassilis Tsotras, Jia Chen, Evangelos E. Papalexakis
arxiv-2410-06408.description: Abstract Hyperparameter optimization is an essential component in many data science pipelines and typically entails exhaustive time and resource-consuming computations in order to explore the combinatorial search space. Similar to this problem, other key operations in data science pipelines exhibit the exact same properties.

arxiv-2512-01639.title: Improved Disease Outbreak Detection from Out-of-sequence measurements Using Markov-switching Fixed-lag Particle Filters
arxiv-2512-01639.creator: Conor Rosato, Joshua Murphy, Siân E. Jenkins, Paul Horridge, Alessandro Varsi, Martyn Bull, Alessandro Gerada, Alex Howard, Veronica Bowman, Simon Maskell
arxiv-2512-01639.description: Abstract Abstract Particle filters (PFs) have become an essential tool for disease surveillance, as they can estimate hidden epidemic states in nonlinear and non-Gaussian models. In epidemic modelling, population dynamics may be governed by distinct regimes such as endemic or outbreak phases which can be represented using Markov-switching state-space models.

arxiv-2601-03573.title: Counting hypertriangles through hypergraph orientations
arxiv-2601-03573.creator: Daniel Paul-Pena, Vaishali Surianarayanan, Deeparnab Chakrabarty, C. Seshadhri
arxiv-2601-03573.description: Abstract . Counting the number of small patterns is a central task in network analysis. While this problem is well studied for graphs, many real-world datasets are naturally modeled as hypergraphs, motivating the need for efficient hypergraph motif counting algorithms. In particular, we study the problem of counting hypertriangles - collections of three pairwise-intersecting hyperedges.

arxiv-2605-17415.title: IVF-TQ: Calibration-Free Streaming Vector Search via a Codebook-Free Residual Layer
arxiv-2605-17415.creator: Tarun Sharma

pmc-10581012.title: Developing a Culturally Appropriate Tool to Support Self-Care in Migrants with Type 2 Diabetes – A Co-Design Study
pmc-10581012.creator: Sara Pettersson, Leonie Klompstra, Maria Jirwe, Tiny Jaarsma
pmc-10581012.description: IntroductionMigrants, especially from the Middle East, experience poorer health outcomes and face greater difficulties in accessing healthcare compared to native populations and there is a need for culturally appropriate education for this vulnerable group. The purpose of this study is to describe the process of developing a culturally appropriate tool to support self-care in migrants with type 2 diabetes.

pmc-10716740.title: A Bayesian noisy logic model for inference of transcription factor activity from single cell and bulk transcriptomic data
pmc-10716740.creator: Argenis Arriojas, Susan Patalano, Jill Macoska, Kourosh Zarringhalam
pmc-10716740.description: The advent of high-throughput sequencing has made it possible to measure the expression of genes at relatively low cost. However, direct measurement of regulatory mechanisms, such as transcription factor (TF) activity is still not readily feasible in a high-throughput manner. Consequently, there is a need for computational approaches that can reliably estimate regulator activity from observable gene expression data.

pmc-10994612.title: Cardamonin mitigates kidney injury by modulating inflammation, oxidative stress, and apoptotic signaling in rats subjected to renal ischemia and reperfusion
pmc-10994612.creator: Haidar Hameed Ali Al-Sultany, Murooj Altimimi, Heider Qassam, Najah Rayish Hadi
pmc-10994612.description: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a critical health concern that aggravates the pathophysiology of acute kidney injury (AKI), leading to high mortality rates in intensive care units. Cardamonin is a natural compound with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. The current study aimed to evaluate the renoprotective impact of cardamonin against AKI induced by renal IRI.

pmc-11510554.title: Preparation and Photocatalytic Performance of In2O3/Bi2WO6 Type II Heterojunction Composite Materials
pmc-11510554.creator: Xiuping Zhang, Fengqiu Qin, Yuanyuan Zhong, Tian Xiao, Qiang Yu, Xiaodong Zhu, Wei Feng, Zhiyong Qi, Xingcai Wu, Lu Lu
pmc-11510554.description: Bismuth-based photocatalytic materials have been widely used in the field of photocatalysis in recent years due to their unique layered structure. However, single bismuth-based photocatalytic materials are greatly limited in their photocatalytic performance due to their poor response to visible light and easy recombination of photogenerated charges.

pmc-11526414.title: Social Media Usage for Medical Education and Smartphone Addiction Among Medical Students: National Web-Based Survey
pmc-11526414.creator: Thomas Clavier, Emma Chevalier, Zoé Demailly, Benoit Veber, Imad-Abdelkader Messaadi, Benjamin Popoff
pmc-11526414.description: BackgroundSocial media (SoMe) have taken a major place in the medical field, and younger generations are increasingly using them as their primary source to find information.ObjectiveThis study aimed to describe the use of SoMe for medical education among French medical students and assess the prevalence of smartphone addiction in this population.

pmc-12595855.title: Association between food addiction and body image dissatisfaction in bariatric surgery candidates: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12595855.creator: Cássia Helena Barroso Jara Maia, Gabriela Mourão Ferreira, Raquel Munhoz Da Silveira Campos, Solange dos Anjos Martins Cravo Fruet Bettini, Laís Nicole Gonçalves Panizzi, Maria Gabriela De Quadros Dlugosz, Mariana Santos Fadanni, Bárbara Dal Molin Netto
pmc-12595855.description: BackgroundThe pursuit of highly palatable foods as a reward can lead to dysfunctional eating behaviors. In bariatric surgery candidates, symptoms of food addiction may impact postoperative weight loss, increase the risk of developing psychological and behavioral disorders, and influence body image perception. The objective was to determine the association between food addiction and body image dissatisfaction in bariatric surgery candidates.

pmc-12727179.title: Applicability of the theory of pain-sensorimotor interactions to orofacial pain and sensorimotor behavior, and implications for orofacial pain research and management
pmc-12727179.creator: Barry J. Sessle, Greg M. Murray
pmc-12727179.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The orofacial sensorimotor system encompasses a variety of orofacial tissues as well as several pathways and circuits in the central nervous system (CNS) that participate in orofacial sensorimotor behaviors such as chewing, facial expression, speech, and swallowing. Acute or chronic pain can severely affect these behaviors, but the relationships between sensorimotor behaviors and pain, and the factors influencing the interactions and underlying mechanisms have remained unclear.

pmc-13338721.title: Description of a new species of the genus Araeopteron Hampson, 1893 (Erebidae, Boletobiinae) from China, with a new subspecies of A. nigrizonatum Hirano, 2021
pmc-13338721.creator: Chun-Hua Yao, Cheng-De Li, Hui-Lin Han
pmc-13338721.description: BackgroundA new species of the genus Araeopteron Hampson, 1893 from China: Araeopteron zheganensis, sp. nov., collected from Zhejiang and Jiangxi Provinces, as well as a new subspecies, A. nigrizonatum chinensis, ssp. nov., recorded from Yunnan, Fujian, Zhejiang and Chongqing.New informationThe study provides illustrations of the adults and genitalia of A. zheganensis, sp. nov. and the new subspecies A.

pmc-13472951.title: Polypill for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: the POLY-HF randomized trial
pmc-13472951.creator: Ambarish Pandey, Neil Keshvani, Syed K. Rizvi, Fatemeh Khashami, Katarina Yaros, Muhammad Shariq Usman, Matthew W. Segar, Anand K. Jain, Juan David Coellar, Myriam Bustillo-Rubio, Zachary L. Cox, Jennifer T. Thibodeau, Chul Ahn, Deepak K. Gupta, Alvin Chandra, Mark H. Drazner, M. Tarique Hussain, Vl
pmc-13472951.description: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction carries a poor prognosis. Although guideline-directed medical therapy reduces morbidity and mortality, its real-world utilization is low. Accordingly, we conducted an open-label randomized trial (POLY-HF) at two centers enrolling a predominantly underserved population to test whether a polypill strategy improves cardiac function in heart failure.

pmc-13549411.title: Association and Age Heterogeneity of Systemic Metabolomic Signatures With Age-Related Cataract: A Mendelian Randomization and Heterogeneity Analysis
pmc-13549411.creator: Zhangluxi Liu, Ao Lu, Siyuan He, Yiying Wang, Guannan Su, Peizeng Yang
pmc-13549411.description: PurposeTo evaluate systemic metabolomic signatures associated with age-related cataract and prioritize signals with age-stable or age-heterogeneous patterns.MethodsWe performed two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses of 249 Nightingale Health metabolomic traits against age-related cataract in FinnGen 12. Higher-confidence MR candidates were defined by inverse-variance weighted (IVW) false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.

pmc-13580975.title: Paediatric perioperative hypersensitivity reactions: Analysis of the French GERAP network database
pmc-13580975.creator: Mertes Paul Michel, Pouessel Guillaume, Gouel Aurélie, Karila Chantal, Lejus‐Bourdeau Corinne, Franchina Sébastien, Tacquard Charles, For the GERAP Network
pmc-13580975.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPerioperative hypersensitivity (POH) reactions are rare but potentially life‐threatening and remain poorly characterised in children. We analysed the largest available French paediatric cohort to describe the epidemiology, causal agents, temporal trends and phenotypes.MethodsWe pooled data from paediatric patients (<18 years) included in six previously published GERAP surveys (1997–2012) and the GERAP computerised database (2017–2024), all evaluated in centres of the GERAP network according to current guidelines.
